stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $S$ be a multiplicative subset of $A$.
Let $\text{Mod}_A$ denote the category of $A$-modules and $\mathcal{T}$ its
Serre subcategory of modules for which any element is annihilated by some
element of $S$. Then there is a canonical equivalence
$\text{Mod}_A/\mathcal{T} \rightarrow \text{Mod}_{S^{-1}A}$.
hypotheses:
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $S$ be a multiplicative subset of $A$.
Let $\text{Mod}_A$ denote the category of $A$-modules and $\mathcal{T}$ its
Serre subcategory of modules for which any element is annihilated by some
element of $S$.

reason: The source establishes that the localization functor on the Serre quotient is faithful and essentially surjective, but does not explicitly prove it is full; those two properties alone do not yield an equivalence without a localization-Hom argument.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $A$ be a Noetherian integral domain. Let $K$ denote its field of fractions.
Let $\text{Mod}_A^{fg}$ denote the category of finitely generated $A$-modules
and $\mathcal{T}^{fg}$ its Serre subcategory of finitely generated torsion
modules. Then $\text{Mod}_A^{fg}/\mathcal{T}^{fg}$ is canonically equivalent
to the category of finite dimensional $K$-vector spaces.
hypotheses:
Let $A$ be a Noetherian integral domain. Let $K$ denote its field of fractions.
Let $\text{Mod}_A^{fg}$ denote the category of finitely generated $A$-modules
and $\mathcal{T}^{fg}$ its Serre subcategory of finitely generated torsion
modules.
conclusions:
$\text{Mod}_A^{fg}/\mathcal{T}^{fg}$ is canonically equivalent
to the category of finite dimensional $K$-vector spaces.

reason: Noetherianity ensures finite A-modules form an abelian category and torsion subobjects of finite modules are finite, so the finite-module Serre quotient embeds fully faithfully in the general localization quotient with image the finite-dimensional K-vector spaces.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
The quotient of the category of abelian groups modulo its
Serre subcategory of torsion groups is the category of
$\mathbf{Q}$-vector spaces.
conclusions:
The quotient of the category of abelian groups modulo its
Serre subcategory of torsion groups is the category of
$\mathbf{Q}$-vector spaces.

reason: Specializes the previously established torsion-module localization equivalence to Z and its field of fractions Q, identifying the quotient category of abelian groups by torsion with rational vector spaces.
